title: Sleep Cycle App – Neumorphism Redesign
lede: An unofficial January 2020 redesign of a sleep-tracking app, made while the trend was weeks old.
summary: Devanta Ebison’s Dribbble concept: an alarm, a sleep journal, and a bar chart pressed into a pale surface with one coral accent.
made: 2020 (posted 2 January 2020, per the Wayback copy of the shot page)

evidence.note: Opened the shot’s image (`dribbble__2x_4x.png`, 1600 × 1200) from cdn.dribbble.com, found through the Wayback capture of 4 January 2020. The live Dribbble page returned an empty body to scripts.

styles.note: A clear example: phones, buttons, tabs, and chart tracks all share one pale surface and differ only by soft raised or pressed shadows; one coral accent marks values and the main action.

context: The designer wrote: “Wanted to try my hand at this new design style called neumorphism because it’s been trending for the past few weeks. This was a fun exercise, but I don’t know if this style will stand the test of time.”
It is a fan concept. Sleep Cycle AB did not make it. The Wayback capture of 4 January 2020 shows 32,152 views and 334 likes.
observed: Three tilted phones on a very pale gray-blue background. The phone bodies, buttons, and tabs are the same color as the background and are shaped by white highlights and soft gray shadows.
The clock display “10:00” sits in a pressed rectangular well; the HR and MIN buttons are raised circles.
The segmented control (Days, Weeks, Months) is a pressed track with a raised pill for the selected item. The chart bars are coral fills inside pressed tracks.
One accent color, a soft coral, fills the “Set alarm” button, the chart bars, the progress rings, and the active tab icon.
Text is a rounded geometric sans-serif in slate gray, bold for figures.
interpretation: A textbook statement of the style two months after [Plyuto’s shot](ref:plyuto-skeuomorph-mobile-banking-2019): the object details are gone, only surface, shadow, and one accent remain. The designer’s own doubt about its future is an early sign of the reaction against it.
borrow: Draw bar-chart tracks as pressed wells and fill them with the accent, so the empty part of each bar stays readable without gridlines.
